Results.ReviewText:
So I bought my first Weber Genesis Grill this past Christmas to replace a 25-year old grill of a different manufacturer that I'd had since new.  It was reliable as a rock, had 3 rebuilds over the years but the poor thing was ready to fall apart.  The Genesis grill was a terrific upgrade and gave me an idea of the quality of the Weber brand.

We got a new travel trailer in January 2022 and we needed a reliable grill to take on our camping excursions.  Naturally, I started looking at a suitable Weber grill to fill that need.  After much looking at all of the various "portable" models I decided on the Q1200 since we didn't really need anything bigger since it's just the wife and myself.

The Q1200 is  a great little grill for our camping excursions.  It's neat and compact and it's almost like they designed it to fit in the storage compartment of our Arctic Fox 25W camper.

I did buy an aftermarket 8-foot braided stainless steel adapter hose to be able to use a 20# propane tank versus the 1# disposable canisters because of the ridiculous cost of the 1# canisters that are about 4X the cost of bulk propane.  The adapter hose still allows the use of the 1# canisters if that is what you have available without any modifications to the grill.

Ultimately, I might modify the grill to hook up directly to the camper's propane system, but that's down the road.  The grill itself works great for 2-3 people though it loses heat very fast when the lid is opened to flip the burgers, hotdogs, chicken or steaks.  You definitely have to cook with the lid closed.  From my experience, you'll get maybe 2-3 grill sessions out of a 1# canister so you'd better take several with you if that is your choice of fuel sources.  With the 20# tank it's not much of a concern as you can lift the tank and readily tell if you have enough fuel for a camping trip.  If it's low, fill the 20# tank up for $10-$12 @ $3/gallon.

Make sure you get spare aluminum pans to catch the drippings out of the bottom of the grill too.  They tend to blow away if it gets windy and they definitely are needed if you're cooking steaks or chicken as the meat tends to drip A LOT!

Results.ReviewText: We purchased the Q1200 to carry along on camping trips.  It's compact, rugged design stores easily when traveling. We use an adapter hose to conncet directly to the propane port on our travel trailer.  The heavy duty cast iron grates pre-heat evenly, and are easy to clean. The side tables make good work areas when the grill is in use and fold nicely for storage.  We have been impressed how well the igniter works, the easy to clean heating surfaces, and rugged design.  The cooking area will handle six good size burgers. It is a good size for a couple, or small family. The cooking surface is similar in size to grills found in many campgrounds. We purchased the Q1200 on the recommendation of other campers. We have a larger Weber grill for home use and felt good about the quality of Weber products based on our past experience. I recommend this grill for couple or small families, especially campers.
Results.Title: Perfect camping grill

ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback. We are sorry to learn that you are having trouble getting your grill to work with the adapter hose and full-sized tank.

We recommend only using a Weber-branded Adapter hose, as others can damage your grill's regulator.

It sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it reduces the pressure. Follow these instructions to reset the bypass safety mode. This is not only the reset, but how you want to light your grill each and every time you use it with an adapter hose.


Open the lid
Make sure the control knob is in the OFF position.
Turn your LP tank on all the way
Wait 60 seconds *This is the MOST IMPORTANT STEP*
Turn the burner to start/high
Hit your igniter
Close the lid
Let your grill preheat to 450 F

We are here to help get you grilling! Please look for an email from our Support team soon.
